title: Sequential approximate isometries: multiplicative mass and target-error growth
question:
Let \(n\ge0\) and let \(H_j=\mathbb C^{d_j}\) with finite \(d_j\ge1\). Core \(j\) is a linear map
\[
V_j:H_{j-1}\longrightarrow\mathbb C^2\otimes H_j\qquad(1\le j\le n).
\]
All spaces carry their standard Euclidean inner products; \(\dagger\) means conjugate transpose and \(\|\cdot\|_{\rm op}\) is the induced operator norm. Rows label outputs and columns label inputs. A new bit is appended after all previously emitted bits, and the bond remains the final tensor factor. Put \(T_0=I_{H_0}\) and, using only the corresponding norm-preserving regrouping,
\[
T_j=(I_{(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes(j-1)}}\otimes V_j)T_{j-1}.
\]
Assume the local Gram defects satisfy
\[
\|V_j^\dagger V_j-I_{H_{j-1}}\|_{\rm op}\le\eta_j,
\qquad 0\le\eta_j<1.
\]
These are approximate linear maps; neither full unitary completions nor a physical channel realization is assumed.

1. Prove a one-step norm-squared inequality valid for every vector on passive emitted bits and the incoming bond, including vectors entangled between those factors. Use it to derive, for every \(v\in H_0\) and every length \(n\),
\[
\prod_{j=1}^n(1-\eta_j)\|v\|_2^2
\le\|T_n v\|_2^2\le
\prod_{j=1}^n(1+\eta_j)\|v\|_2^2.
\]
Give the resulting bound on \(\|T_n^\dagger T_n-I\|_{\rm op}\). Show that the two mass endpoints can each be attained by legal bond-dimension-one trains. Do not replace the product by \(1\pm\sum_j\eta_j\) as an exact general inequality without justification.

2. Does zero defect at every stage imply fidelity to a specified target train? Give two legal one-stage, bond-dimension-one trains with zero defects whose outputs from initial scalar 1 are orthogonal. State exactly what Gram/mass control therefore certifies and what target information it lacks.

3. In this separate comparison branch, suppose additional maps \(W_j:H_{j-1}\to\mathbb C^2\otimes H_j\) are exact isometries, \(W_j^\dagger W_j=I\), and \(\|V_j-W_j\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_j\) with \(\epsilon_j\ge0\). Let \(S_n\) be their sequential composition in the same order as \(T_n\). For a unit vector \(v\), prove the growth-weighted target bound
\[
\|T_n v-S_n v\|_2
\le\sum_{k=1}^n\epsilon_k\prod_{j=k+1}^n\sqrt{1+\eta_j}.
\]
Explain why the product weights involve stages later than the inserted discrepancy. Give a two-stage, bond-dimension-one example satisfying all stated premises for which the simpler claim \(\|T_2v-S_2v\|_2\le\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2\) fails. This is an unnormalized vector bound; no normalization or postselection is implicit.

4. Check the empty chain, zero input, and the exact-isometry specialization. Separately replace the strict local condition by \(\eta_j=1\) and show why a positive lower mass is then not guaranteed. Explain why these conclusions alone give neither a unitary-circuit synthesis theorem nor terminal-bond cleanup. Each diagnostic must state which premises it retains or replaces.
evidence_boundary: These frozen nodes ground exact source definitions and conventions only. The requested perturbative/numerical statements are original natural-language targets, not claimed existing compiled theorem statements.
assumptions: Finite nonzero complex bond spaces with standard Euclidean inner products and dimension-compatible core maps.
For the main mass branch, each local operator Gram defect is bounded by 0<=eta_j<1.
Only the comparison branch receives exact ideal isometries W_j and operator differences bounded by epsilon_j; unit input is required only for its displayed absolute error budget.
The eta_j=1 diagnostic replaces the strict defect premise; the zero-input diagnostic does not retain the comparison branch unit-input premise.
conventions: Each core maps an incoming column vector to a new-bit and outgoing-bond column vector; emitted bits are ordered chronologically and the bond is last.
Adjoint is conjugate transpose; all norms are induced Euclidean norms and the tensor regrouping is norm-preserving.
Gram control concerns unnormalized linear maps; it does not by itself define a physical probability-preserving channel or clean terminal register.
All empty products equal one and empty sums equal zero.
